title: Reading Drill — Mapping an old village well — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Mapping an old village well — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The heritage researcher had been asked to investigate different records placing the well on opposite sides of a road in Elmbrook. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the distance between recorded positions, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a three-week comparison, the team used historic surveys at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because changes in the name of the road might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a matched overlay of field maps. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
